topics.topic: 1. Basic concepts of forest and forestry
topics.notes: Meaning of forest and forestry. Differences between Forestry and Agriculture (land occupancy, time frame, risk, etc.) and business aspects of forestry. Functions of the forest; types of plants in the forest (trees, shrubs, herbs, climbers, special plants); local and botanical names of timber trees.

subtopics.notes: Characteristics of the Forest environment; physical components; meaning of forest ecology. Plant habitats (aquatic, terrestrial, arboreal) and types of plants in them. Types of animals in the forest and their habitat characteristics.

Meaning of ecosystem and examples/types (aquatic, terrestrial, arboreal). Major components and functions. Food chains, food webs, producer-consumer relationships, symbiotic associations. Differences between saprophytes and epiphytes.
Regulation, supporting, cultural functions. Effects of good and degraded ecosystems on health.

Characteristics of major vegetation zones and types in West Africa. Comparisons in plant species. Typical plants, animals, and associations. Vegetation types: Wet-evergreen, Moist-evergreen, Moist semi-deciduous, Dry semi-deciduous, Mangroves, Savannah.
Climatic (rainfall, temperature), Edaphic (soil), Biotic factors.

Distribution, Composition and Structure of Tropical High Forest (rain forest, moist semi-deciduous), Savannah, Coastal Scrub and Grassland. Characteristics of virgin/primeval, secondary, natural, artificial forests. Land use practices in different zones.

subtopics.subtopic: (d) Major Forest Types in Relation to Latitudes
subtopics.notes: Tropical, Temperate Coniferous, Arctic. Relationship between temperature and latitude. Characteristics and distribution of angiosperms and gymnosperms.
Understanding of the term wildlife and wildlife resources in Ghana.
Common and scientific names of wildlife species.
Socio-economy, Environment, Forestry, Tourism, Scientific research.

subtopics.subtopic: (d) Endangered, Rare and Common Wildlife Species
subtopics.notes: Examples (e.g., Elephants - Endangered, Porcupine - Rare, grasscutter - Common) and reasons.

Types in Ghana: National Parks (e.g., Mole, Kakum, Bui), Game Production Reserves (e.g., Shai Hills), Wildlife Sanctuaries (e.g., Buabeng-Fiema, Owabi), Strict Nature Reserves (e.g., Digya). Features and locations.
Management of reserves and zoos; protection against poachers.
Morphological and anatomical features (leaf, stem, roots; xylem, phloem, cambium, epidermis, cortex, pith).
Observable features (leaves, bark, buttress, stem). Local/trade names, scientific names, and scientific nomenclature.

topics.notes: Processes for Reservation and Constitution; role of Reserve Settlement Commissioner; Internal and External Pillaring; Admitted Rights. Differences between Protected and Non-protected forests.

Systems of Management and Development of Public and Private Estates. Problems (Bushfires, Illegal farming, Illegal felling, Chainsawing, Illegal mining) and solutions. Bushfires as management problem and tool.
Historical facts of Ghana’s forest (area, composition, depletion trend due to population growth).
Measures against over-exploitation: Ban on log exports, Star rating of species, Differential stumpage fees, Participatory forestry, Yield selection, Permits and felling rights.
